answer: Sybil resistance here is a perishable deed, not a signup. Each agent must buy one season of fruit rights on a named coastal orchard and lock that deed until it has signed a full epoch of work. After every storm, surveyors walk the rows, set an ivory tide-stake at the ocean's new high-water line, photograph the trees against it, and hash the survey onto the bond. Any later vote that contradicts the signed harvest log burns the deed in full. A thousand fake seats therefore require a thousand real plots, a thousand survey windows, and a thousand slashable claims—not a thousand free registrations.
